title: A second finger while drawing restarts the stroke and orphans a 60 Hz flush timer
body:
## Summary
The pad started a new stroke on every pointerdown, even with a stroke open, in companion/index.html.

## Description
pointerdown (companion/index.html:404) never checked `drawing`. A second finger or a palm sent a second pen `down` over the live stroke (PenEngine.handlePen clears the live stroke on a new down, so the first ink vanished on the TV) and overwrote flushTimer with a new setInterval, leaving the first 60 Hz timer running for the life of the tab. Fixed: a pointerdown while a stroke is open is ignored.

## Flow
- finger 1 draws; finger 2 touches the pad
- pointerdown -> flush("down") again, flushTimer = setInterval(...) again
- TV drops stroke 1; phone keeps an orphan interval

## Expected impact
Anyone drawing with a phone held in the hand (palm contact) keeps their stroke; the tab stops running a stray timer. Could break: a deliberate two-finger gesture on the pad (none exists).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one stroke per gesture, no orphan timer
Before: CDP multi-touch: 2 pen downs, 1 interval left running
After: 1 down, 0 intervals
Method: gate - companion-refusal-test "two fingers", red then green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: companion/index.html:404 pointerdown had no `if (drawing) return`; :426 flushTimer = setInterval(() => flush("move"), 16) overwrote the previous id; core PenEngine.kt handlePen "down" -> clearLive()

title: The pressed rate button is the last tap, not the rate the TV reports
body:
## Summary
applyState ignored state.rate, so the rate row showed a local guess (companion/index.html:323).

## Description
Every heartbeat carries rate (core Protocol.kt TvMessage.State.rate) and the TV keeps it across phones (tv-app Session.rate). The page set aria-pressed only on its own clicks (radio("rates")), so a phone opened on a TV in slow motion showed 1x pressed, and a tap dropped while disconnected stayed pressed. Registry: realtime-events push-vs-refetch-reconciliation. Fixed: applyState sets the pressed rate from m.rate.

## Flow
- TV at 0.25x (remote, earlier phone)
- a phone opens the page
- state.rate=0.25 arrives; 1x stays pressed

## Expected impact
The viewer sees the speed the TV is actually playing at. Could break: nothing; a rate the row does not offer shows none pressed.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the rate shown is the rate played
Before: fake TV at 0.25: 1x pressed
After: 0.25x pressed
Method: gate - companion-refusal-test "rate", red then green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: grep "m.rate" companion/index.html (before): 0 hits; core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/Protocol.kt State(rate: Double); tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/Session.kt:54 var rate

title: Moving the scrub bar by keyboard or screen reader never seeks the TV
body:
## Summary
The seek was sent only after a pointerdown had set `scrubbing` (companion/index.html:603).

## Description
endScrub returned unless pointerdown set scrubbing; arrow keys, switch access and TalkBack swipe-to-adjust move a range input with no pointer, so the bar moved, nothing reached the TV, and the next heartbeat snapped it back. Fixed: a change with no pointer in progress is the seek; a pointer drag is deduplicated to one seek until the TV next moves the bar.

## Flow
- focus the scrub bar
- press ArrowRight five times
- no transport seek is sent; the heartbeat resets the bar

## Expected impact
Screen-reader and keyboard users can seek. Could break: a pointer drag sending two seeks (guarded).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a non-pointer adjust seeks
Before: 5 ArrowRight presses: 0 seeks
After: 5 seeks, last at 100 ms; pointer drag still 1 seek (seeded: 2 without dedupe, red)
Method: gate - companion-refusal-test "scrub" + GUARD, red then green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: companion/index.html:603-611 endScrub `if (!scrubbing) return;` with scrubbing set only at :598 on pointerdown

title: The companion's offline browser suite had no runner at all
body:
## Summary
tools/companion-refusal-test.mjs (no device needed) was run by no script, stage or workflow.

## Description
The suite pins refusal, reconnect, fragment PIN and now multi-touch, rate, scrub and unpaired controls against a fake TV in headless Chromium. grep over .github/, desk/package.json, tools/package.json and scripts/ found 0 runners. Registry: test-harness out-of-graph-artifacts. Fixed: dev.ps1's unit stage runs it after :core:test (Initialize-LiveTools first, exit code judged, about 9 s) and tools/ has `npm run test:companion`; device-rules-test pins both.

## Flow
- edit companion/index.html
- run dev.ps1 or any gate
- the page's 26 behaviours were never checked

## Expected impact
The operator's cycle catches a companion regression before a device run. Could break: dev.ps1 unit now needs tools/ packages and Chromium (installed once by Initialize-LiveTools).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the suite runs somewhere
Before: 0 runners
After: 2 (dev.ps1 unit/all, npm script); guard red then green
Method: gate - device-rules-test "the companion suite has a runner"
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: grep -rn companion-refusal .github desk/package.json tools/package.json scripts -> no hit (before)

title: prevT is written on every heartbeat and read nowhere
body:
## Summary
A dead variable in the page's state handler (companion/index.html:174, :331).

## Description
prevT was assigned from each state message and never read. Zero-consumer grep: only its declaration and its own assignment in companion/index.html; no hit in tools/, tv-app/, core/. Removed.

## Flow
- grep prevT
- declaration + self-assignment only
- remove both

## Expected impact
One less piece of misleading state to read around. Could break: nothing (suite 25/25 before and after).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - dead state removed
Before: 1 dead variable, 2 sites
After: 0
Method: gate - companion-refusal-test 25/25 both sides, zero-consumer grep
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: grep -n prevT companion/index.html -> :174 declaration, :336 `if (m.t !== (prevT ?? -1)) { prevT = m.t; }`; git grep prevT tools tv-app core -> none

title: TV controls took presses while no TV held the pen
body:
## Summary
Clear, Clear all, Play, frame steps, rates and scrub stayed enabled while connecting, refused or replaced.

## Description
send() drops everything without an open socket (companion/index.html:198) and nothing reaches the TV before its welcome, yet nine controls kept taking presses: a rate showed pressed, the bar moved, Clear flashed, and the TV changed nothing. Registry: ui-controls micro-interaction-contracts. Fixed: tvControls(false) until the welcome and on any close or refusal; undo/redo/drawing steps still wait for state; the pen's tools and colours stay live.

## Flow
- open the page with a wrong PIN
- press Clear all or 0.5x
- the press looks taken; nothing is sent

## Expected impact
A viewer is never told by the UI that an unsent command happened. Could break: a control left disabled after pairing (guarded: 9 back live).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - no false acknowledgement
Before: 9 TV controls live on a refused page
After: 0; 9 live again after the right PIN; 0 pen tools disabled
Method: gate - companion-refusal-test "unpaired", red then green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: companion/index.html:198 send() `if (connected)`; nav rows at :122-152 had no disabled state tied to `paired`

title: No CI workflow runs the companion's offline browser suite
body:
## Summary
companion-refusal-test now runs in dev.ps1 and an npm script, but no .github workflow runs it on a PR.

## Description
A PR that edits companion/index.html is gated by :core:test (CompanionContractTest, wire contract only) and nothing else; the 26 browser checks run only when the operator runs dev.ps1. The workflows are outside this round's paths (.github/), so this is out-of-scope for the round, Lane B.

## Flow
- add a job that installs tools/ and Chromium
- run node tools/companion-refusal-test.mjs
- seed a red on a branch and confirm the job fails

## Expected impact
A companion regression is caught on the PR. Could break: CI minutes (about 1 min for the Chromium install, cached thereafter).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - PR gate covers the phone page
Before: 0 workflows run it
After: not built: a workflow is outside the round
Method: simulation - the suite runs offline in 9 s here; a runner needs Chromium
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence: grep -rn companion-refusal .github/ -> no hit; AGENTS.md "quality.yml runs the desk gate and :core:test on every PR"
instrument: a quality.yml (or harness-drills.yml) job: npm ci --prefix tools, npx playwright install chromium, node tools/companion-refusal-test.mjs; seed a red by reverting 6bcbbadb on a branch and watch the job fail

title: A refused, locked or replaced pen changes only a status line no screen reader announces
body:
## Summary
#status has no live region; "wrong PIN", the lockout countdown and "another phone has the pen" are silent to TalkBack.

## Description
#status (companion/index.html:79) is a plain span rewritten on every heartbeat (applyState, every 400 ms) and on each refusal. Marking it aria-live would announce the clock constantly; the fix is a separate polite region for pairing events only (refusal, lockout start/end, takeover, reconnect). Needs a measured design: what is announced and how often.

## Flow
- pair with a wrong PIN under TalkBack
- the PIN box appears; nothing is spoken
- a takeover by another phone is equally silent

## Expected impact
A blind viewer learns why the pen stopped. Could break: chatter if the region also gets heartbeat text.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - pairing changes are announced
Before: 0 live regions
After: not built
Method: simulation - read the page; the announcement count needs the instrument
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence: grep -n "aria-live\|role=\"status\"" companion/index.html -> none; companion/index.html:324 applyState rewrites #status every heartbeat
instrument: Playwright accessibility snapshot / a MutationObserver over aria-live regions during a refusal, a lockout countdown and a takeover, plus 10 s of heartbeats: count announcements per event (want 1 per refusal, 0 per heartbeat)
